name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments-Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
one_sentence_pitch: A series of experiments is proposed with the following specific objectives, in both soot-free and sooty flames, to compare with detailed computational simulation to assess transport properties and detailed chemical kinetics (including chemiluminescence): Objec
plain_summary: A series of experiments is proposed with the following specific objectives, in both soot-free and sooty flames, to compare with detailed computational simulation to assess transport properties and detailed chemical kinetics (including chemiluminescence): Objective A. Measure and characterize the transient structure (such as temperature and species distribution) of diffusion flames established at initially non-steady, spherical flame structures for mixtures of different H2/CH4/diluent ratios (soot-free) and different C2H4/diluent ratios (sooty), for different flow rates. Determine the quasi-steady convective/chemical-kinetic extinction limits (low system Damköhler numbers) and radiative/chemical-kinetic extinction limits (high system Damköhler numbers) for mixtures of different H2/CH4/diluent ratios (soot-free) and different C2H4/diluent ratios (sooty).
objectives: A series of experiments is proposed with the following specific objectives, in both soot-free and sooty flames, to compare with detailed computational simulation to assess transport properties and detailed chemical kinetics (including chemiluminescence): Objective A.

Measure and characterize the transient structure (such as temperature and species distribution) of diffusion flames established at initially non-steady, spherical flame structures for mixtures of different H2/CH4/diluent ratios (soot-free) and different C2H4/diluent ratios (sooty), for different flow rates.

Determine the quasi-steady convective/chemical-kinetic extinction limits (low system Damköhler numbers) and radiative/chemical-kinetic extinction limits (high system Damköhler numbers) for mixtures of different H2/CH4/diluent ratios (soot-free) and different C2H4/diluent ratios (sooty).

Determine the existence (for different Zeldovich number, Ze), onset (as a function Da), and nature (i.e. mode, frequency, amplitude) of pulsating instabilities theoretically predicted to occur in transient spherical diffusion flames using fuel/diluent mixtures that are above a critical Lewis number.
method: A series of experiments is proposed in which mixtures of various gaseous fuels and diluents will be issued into an oxidizing environment through a spherical porous burner and ignited to obtain, nominally, a spherical, one-dimensional stabilized flame. Synchronized measurements are to be made including spectrally resolved images, flame and burner temperatures, radiative flux measurements, and system operating conditions (including reactant flow rates, ambient temperatures, pressures and acceleration levels, etc.). These data are to be used for comparisons of flame behavior and structure with detailed numerical simulations of the flames.
main_findings: The impact of this work consists of both practical and fundamental aspects.

Practically, with diffusion flame burning as the basis in many combustion engines and devices, understanding the underlying dynamics and chemistry of diffusion flames is important in improving performance in terms of power, efficiency, pollutant emissions, and reliability.

Fundamentally, the unique buoyancy-free environment offered by microgravity affords simple aerodynamic flow fields to acquire diffusion flame data of high fidelity, with the prospect of understanding unit thermochemical processes as well as quantifying the associated physico-chemical parameters.
safety_relevance: Supports NASA’s prevention pillar of spacecraft fire safety.
